claim: Composer's TQQQ RSI Strategy page states the full rule in plain English -- a 200-day trend filter, RSI and PPO speed checks, TQQQ bought on dips and SHV held otherwise, with SQQQ or UVXY after extreme up days and TECL on deep sell-offs -- and reports a 68.9% annualized return with Sharpe 1.46 over the whole 2011-10-04 backtest, against roughly 41% annualized out of sample.
limitations: Composer's discovery page shows winners only, the author can edit the recipe and reset the out-of-sample start, and the headline blends in-sample with out-of-sample history. The page does not disclose the exact PPO parameters, so the replication uses the disclosed 200-day trend and RSI(10) branches only.
quote: Daily, it rotates among a few ETFs based on price signals: - Trend filter: only buy during uptrends (price above its 200‑day average). - “Speed” checks: RSI (0–100; low=oversold, high=overheated) and PPO (short vs long averages; below 0=weak). - Core: buy TQQQ (3x Nasdaq‑100) on dips; park in SHV (short‑term Treasuries) otherwise. - After extreme up days/overheating, briefly use SQQQ (−3x Nasdaq‑100) or UVXY (VIX/fear). - Sometimes buy TECL (3x Tech) on deep sell‑offs.

claim: Composer's TQQQ Safe Strategy page discloses the whole decision tree -- QQQ above its 200-day average holds TQQQ at 100% when strong or 70/30 with T-bills when softer, buys dips at RSI below 30 and moves to T-bills when RSI is above 78 or price is below the 50-day average -- and reports 56.26% annualized with Sharpe 1.28 since 2022-12-28.
limitations: Same platform caveats as the page above; the out-of-sample start is 2026-03-29, so its OOS record is under six months and the headline is mostly in-sample.
quote: Trades: QQQ (Nasdaq‑100, big tech), TQQQ (3× QQQ), SQQQ (−3× QQQ), and a T‑bill fund (cash‑like). If QQQ > 200‑day avg, it holds TQQQ (100% if strong; 70%/30% with T‑bills if softer), buys dips (RSI<30), and shifts to T‑bills if overheated (RSI>78) or <50‑day avg. If QQQ < 200‑day avg, it holds T‑bills; may use 50% SQQQ when falling, or 25% TQQQ when steadier. RSI=0–100 “heat” gauge.

claim: Composer's TQQQ FTLT 2.0 page discloses a two-state tree -- SPY above its 200-day average is risk-on and rotates into volatility funds when tech is very hot, otherwise rides leveraged Nasdaq; below trend it buys deeply oversold leveraged rebounds or holds whichever of SQQQ and TLT is stronger -- and targets roughly 29.7% annualized out of sample versus 20% for the S&P.
limitations: Winners-only discovery page; the risk-off leg's exact oversold threshold is not published, so the replication uses the same RSI(10) < 30 rule as the other F1 cells.
quote: Trend: if SPY > 200‑day avg = risk‑on; else risk‑off. RSI = 0–100 heat of recent moves (high=overbought, low=oversold). Risk‑on: if tech is very hot, rotate into volatility (UVXY/VIXY) unless they just crashed; otherwise ride Nasdaq with leverage (prefer TQQQ; if weaker, QQQ/QLD), only flipping to VIXY on fear spikes. Risk‑off: buy brief rebounds (TECL/UPRO) when deeply oversold; else hold SQQQ (short tech) or TLT (Treasuries), whichever is stronger. Tickers: QQQ=Nasdaq‑100; TQQQ 3x; QLD 2x; SQQQ −3x; SPXL/UPRO 3x S&P; TECL 3x; VIXY/UVXY=volatility; TLT=bonds.

claim: Allocate Smartly publishes Accelerating Dual Momentum's complete rule set for free: at each month end average each of SPY's and SCZ's 1, 3 and 6-month total returns, hold whichever is higher if it is also positive, and otherwise hold whichever of TLT and TIP has the higher 1-month return, holding until the next month end.
limitations: The page publishes rules but not current performance, so there is no public recent benchmark to compare our numbers against; Allocate Smartly does not track leveraged variants at all, so the 3x cell has no public record by construction.
quote: At the close on the last trading day of the month, calculate a “momentum score” for two asset classes: the S&P 500 (represented by SPY ) and international small cap equities ( SCZ ), by averaging each asset’s 1, 3 and 6-month total return. If the momentum score of SPY > SCZ and > 0, go long SPY at the close. If the momentum score of SCZ > SPY and > 0, go long SCZ at the close. If neither condition is true, go long either long-term US Treasuries ( TLT ) or US TIPS ( TIP ), whichever has the highest 1-month return. Hold position until the final trading day of the following month.

claim: Allocate Smartly publishes Bold Asset Allocation in full: a canary universe of SPY, EFA, EEM and AGG scored with 13612W momentum, any negative score sending the whole book to the defensive universe, selection inside each universe by the slower p0/average(p0..p12) relative momentum, one offensive asset for the aggressive version and six for the balanced one, three defensive assets, and any defensive asset weaker than BIL parked in cash.
limitations: Allocate Smartly itself flags BAA as carrying overfitting risk and says it prefers Hybrid Asset Allocation; the current performance figures are behind its paywall.
quote: Start with the canary universe: S&P 500 (represented by SPY), developed intl equities (EFA), emerging market equities (EEM) and US aggregate bonds (AGG). Calculate the “13612W” momentum of each asset. This is a multi-timeframe measure of momentum, calculated as follows: (12 * (p0 / p1 – 1)) + (4 * (p0 / p3 – 1)) + (2 * (p0 / p6 – 1)) + (p0 / p12 – 1) Where p0 = the price at today’s close, p1 = the price at the close of the previous month, etc.

claim: Lin (2025, Applied Economics and Finance 12(3):30-46) reports a statistically significant positive Monday-to-Tuesday and negative Friday-to-next-Monday overnight return in US large caps and index ETFs, and builds a trading model that buys before the close and sells at the next open while skipping Wednesday and/or Friday.
limitations: The abstract does not state a cost assumption, and the census recorded a headline Sharpe of 7.75, which is implausible net of real spreads. This sweep charges the frozen 10 and 20 bp per side, which is almost certainly stricter than the paper's.
quote: This paper provides a comprehensive study of the weekly seasonality of the overnight effect in US large-cap stocks and index exchange-traded funds (ETFs). We identify a distinct pattern: a statistically significant positive Monday-to-Tuesday and negative Friday-to-next-Monday overnight (close to next open) return in large-cap US equities and index ETFs. We find overnight effect exhibits statistically significant patterns depending on the day of the week. This paper focuses on the weekly seasonality of this effect, exploring how the overnight return patterns vary across the weekdays. A short-term trading model is built to buy these stocks and ETFs before the market close and sell at the opening of the next trading day, and skips Wednesday and/or Friday.

claim: Quantpedia's sector momentum rotational system entry states the rule as picking the three sector ETFs with the strongest 12-month momentum, weighting them equally and rebalancing monthly, and reports a Sharpe ratio of 0.54 with a -46.29% maximum drawdown for the top-three variant.
limitations: Quantpedia summarises an academic source rather than running a live book; the 0.54 Sharpe is a long-history number and says nothing about 2023-2026.
quote: Use ten sector ETFs. Pick 3 ETFs with the strongest 12-month momentum into your portfolio and weight them equally. Hold them for one month and then rebalance.
